evals.prompt:
Hey — between roles right now, senior FE dev (Angular, 7y, NgRx, strict TS, EU/Slovakia, prefer B2B contracts). Just got this posting forwarded by a friend. Worth applying?

---

Senior Frontend Engineer @ ViaBill (Copenhagen, fully remote EU)

About us: BNPL fintech, $150M+ annual transactions, backed by Headline and BlackFin Capital Partners.

Stack: Angular 20+, NgRx, TypeScript strict, Jest. Node.js/Express backend, AWS.

You will:
- Build and ship customer-facing features in the BNPL flow
- Own pieces of the frontend architecture and contribute to backend services
- Pair with product to shape features, not just implement them
- Take part in on-call rotation for the platform

We want:
- 5+ years frontend, senior Angular (signals, standalone, strict TS)
- Hands-on Node.js / Express experience for backend collaboration — must-have
- Comfortable with AWS
- Production on-call experience

Bonus: experience with payments / BNPL, NgRx SignalStore, modern AI-assisted dev workflows.

Compensation: competitive, depending on experience.
---

what do you think?
evals.expected_output: Fit analysis with a clear verdict, identifies Node/Express as hard gap, asks for CV, writes posting.md + fit-analysis.md.

assertions.text: Identifies Node.js/Express as the binding hard-requirement gap
Recognizes senior Angular + NgRx + strict TS as strong matches
Calls out on-call expectation and probes user fit for it
Notes the missing compensation range as something to clarify in screen
Surfaces user-strength bonus matches (Signals / NgRx / AI workflows)
Produces an explicit verdict (Apply / Apply with caveats / Skip)
If applying, gives specific advice for framing the Node gap
Asks for the user's CV OR runs an onboarding flow because no profile exists
Saves the posting verbatim to a file in applications/<slug>/posting.md
Saves a fit analysis to a file in applications/<slug>/fit-analysis.md
Final chat response stays under ~600 words (concision)

evals.prompt:
a recruiter just emailed me about a contractor role. need to reply soon but don't want to commit to a rate before I even talked to anyone. here's the email — help me draft something?

'Hi Matej,

Reaching out about a Senior Frontend Engineer role with one of our clients (large Slovak fintech, can't disclose yet). 6-month initial contract, remote with one day/week in Bratislava.

Budget is 250-300 EUR/day. We'd be proposing 275. Can you confirm you're happy with this range and send your CV by EOD?

Also — given the speed they want to move, we'd need exclusive representation for this client. Client wants to interview Monday.

Best, Ronnie
Wave Talent'
evals.expected_output: Drafted reply that doesn't commit on 275, scopes exclusivity, sends CV, concise, no filler softeners.

assertions.text: Drafted reply does NOT confirm or accept the 275 EUR/day rate
Drafted reply addresses exclusivity by scoping to this specific client/opportunity rather than blanket
Drafted reply mentions sending CV
Drafted reply does NOT contain filler softeners (e.g. 'happy to wait', 'no rush', 'whenever convenient', 'at your earliest convenience')
Drafted reply is concise (under ~150 words)
Parses the incoming email structurally before drafting (extracts client info, budget, exclusivity ask, urgency)
Notes the rate-anchor-low pattern (recruiter proposing 275 from a 250-300 range)
Provides explanation/coaching to the user about why the specific deflection wording works
Output is in English (matching user's input language)

evals.prompt: Got a take-home for a senior FE role at Hospitable.com (Airbnb host SaaS). 2.5 hours, build a cart + checkout flow with a credit card form, Angular + NgRx required. They explicitly said 'use AI tools as you would normally'. How should I approach this — particularly the card form part, given they're a fintech-ish company?
evals.expected_output: Strategy with time allocation, AI usage discipline, README requirements, card form specifics + PCI tokenization callout, saves to take-home.md.

assertions.text: Mentions PCI / tokenization / Stripe Elements (or equivalent SDK) for production card handling
Provides explicit time allocation across phases (plan / scaffold / core / polish / submit)
Names specific senior signals for the card form (Luhn validation, expiry check, autocomplete attrs, inputmode)
Addresses AI usage discipline beyond 'just use AI' (e.g. 'you direct, AI implements' or what to delegate vs own)
Specifies README content with named sections (architectural decisions, AI usage log, trade-offs, setup)
Addresses testing philosophy that avoids trivial tests (e.g. tests on real logic, not boilerplate)
Saves take-home strategy notes to applications/<slug>/take-home.md
Reads the prompt as evaluating senior signals (not just 'build feature X')
Final chat response is structured (lists / sections), not a wall of prose
